name: Start a fire with a hand drill
blurb: The bow drill without the bow: bare hands spinning a long spindle. It demands better materials, drier conditions and tougher hands than any other friction method.
gear: A long, straight, dead-dry spindle: mullein, horseweed, elderberry
steps: Select a spindle 60–75 cm long, straight and bone dry — moisture that a bow drill tolerates will defeat you here.
Burn in a socket and cut the collection notch exactly as for a bow drill.
Learn the float: spin with your palms while travelling down the spindle, then snap your hands back to the top without stopping the spin.
Build heat in long sets rather than frantic ones, keeping constant downward pressure through your palms.
Finish with a fast, heavy set until the dust pile smokes on its own.
Transfer to tinder and blow to flame.
tips: Blisters mean you are sliding rather than pressing. Toughen your hands gradually over weeks.
A thumb loop or a helper on the second set is legitimate practice, not cheating.
This method is genuinely hard in damp climates. Master the bow drill first.
proof: An ember from hand-drill alone, blown to flame, with no bow involved.
